validation.output: Complete every field with a valid number.

multi_peril.name: Multi-Peril Crop Insurance (MPCI)
multi_peril.desc: Traditional indemnity-based. Insures against multiple risks — drought, flood, hail, pest, disease. Pays based on actual farm-level loss assessment.
multi_peril.pros: Covers actual farm-level losses. Payout based on real damage.
multi_peril.cons: Higher premiums. Requires field assessment (slow payouts 4–8 weeks). Moral hazard risk.

area_yield_index.name: Area Yield Index Insurance
area_yield_index.desc: Pays when the AVERAGE yield in an area falls below a threshold. No individual farm assessment needed.
area_yield_index.pros: Cheaper. Faster payouts. Less moral hazard.
area_yield_index.cons: Basis risk — your farm may lose but area average is fine (no payout).

weather_index.name: Weather Index Insurance (WII)
weather_index.desc: Pays when a weather parameter (rainfall, temperature) crosses a threshold using satellite or station data. No farm visit required.
weather_index.pros: Fastest payouts — often automatic via mobile money within 2 weeks. Cheapest to administer.
weather_index.cons: Basis risk — weather at station may differ from your farm. Does not cover all risks (e.g. pests).

livestock_index.name: Index-Based Livestock Insurance (IBLI)
livestock_index.desc: Covers livestock mortality due to drought using NDVI satellite vegetation index. No individual animal assessment.
livestock_index.pros: Covers pastoralists with large herds. Satellite-triggered payouts within 2 weeks.
livestock_index.cons: Basis risk. Only covers drought-related deaths, not disease or accident.

programs.name: NAIC Agricultural Insurance
programs.enrollHow: Visit NAIC state offices or Bank of Agriculture (BOA) branches. Compulsory for government loan recipients.
programs.notes: Covers crops and livestock. Government pays 50% of your premium. Compulsory for farmers accessing BOA/government loans.

programs.name: Pula (formerly ACRE Africa)
programs.enrollHow: Often bundled with certified seed or fertilizer purchases. Ask your agro-dealer.
programs.notes: Satellite-based. Payout triggered automatically — no claim form needed. Premium sometimes embedded in input price.

programs.name: ACRE Africa / Pula
programs.enrollHow: Purchase certified seed bundled with insurance, or enroll via M-Pesa Insurance menu. Kenya Agricultural Insurance Programme (KAIP) subsidizes premium.
programs.notes: Over 2M farmers covered. Satellite rainfall data — no farm visit. Government subsidizes 50% through KAIP.

programs.name: IBLI — Index-Based Livestock Insurance
programs.enrollHow: Available for pastoralists in Turkana, Marsabit, Isiolo, Wajir counties through Takaful Insurance branches.
programs.notes: Landmark program. Global model for pastoralist insurance. Covers cattle, camels, shoats (sheep + goats).

programs.name: Multi-Peril Crop Insurance (MPCI)
programs.provider: Santam Agri / Old Mutual Agriculture / Mutual & Federal
programs.enrollHow: Contact Santam Agri, Old Mutual Agriculture, or Mutual & Federal brokers. Most commercial farmers use short-term insurers.
programs.notes: Most developed agri-insurance market in Africa. No government subsidy — fully commercial. High penetration among commercial farmers.

programs.name: Crop Hail Insurance
programs.enrollHow: Available through agricultural brokers. Very common in Highveld maize/wheat belt where hail is frequent.
programs.notes: Narrow cover but very cost-effective for hail-prone regions. Often combined with MPCI.

programs.name: GAIP — Ghana Agricultural Insurance Programme
programs.provider: Ghana Agricultural Insurance Pool (consortium of licensed insurers)
programs.enrollHow: Enroll through banks linked to Planting for Food & Jobs programme, or GAIP member insurance companies.
programs.notes: Government subsidizes 50% of premium through the Ministry of Food & Agriculture. Linked to PFJ agri-input subsidy programme.

programs.name: PBDAC Crop Insurance
programs.provider: Principal Bank for Development and Agricultural Credit (PBDAC) + insurance companies
programs.enrollHow: Bundled automatically with PBDAC agricultural crop loans. Standalone enrollment at PBDAC branches across Egypt.
programs.notes: Egypt has the oldest agri-insurance program in Africa. Significant government subsidy — farmers pay only ~30% of gross premium. Covers Nile Valley and Delta irrigated farms.

programs.name: R4 Rural Resilience Initiative
programs.enrollHow: Join community groups in Tigray, Amhara, SNNPR that participate in WFP's R4 programme. Premium is paid through community work (food-for-work).
programs.notes: Innovative — farmers pay premium through community labor on watershed rehabilitation. No cash needed. Limited to R4 programme areas.

programs.name: EAIC Crop Insurance
programs.enrollHow: Apply at EAIC offices or through banks linked to Ethiopian agricultural credit programs.
programs.notes: Government-backed. Linked to ADLI agricultural development program. Premium subsidy varies by region.

programs.name: ACRE Africa Tanzania
programs.enrollHow: Bundled with certified seeds at agro-dealers, or via M-Pesa insurance menu. Government of Tanzania subsidizes through ASDP.
programs.notes: Active in maize and rice belts of Dodoma, Iringa, Morogoro. Satellite-based — no field assessment needed.

programs.name: Tanzania Agricultural Development Bank (TADB) Crop Insurance
programs.enrollHow: Apply through TADB branches when accessing agricultural loans. Also available through NIC Tanzania offices.
programs.notes: Linked to TADB agricultural credit. Subsidy provided through Ministry of Agriculture.

programs.name: Uganda Agricultural Insurance Scheme (UAIS)
programs.enrollHow: Apply through UAIS member insurance companies or at Ministry of Agriculture (MAAIF) offices. Linked to government agricultural loans.
programs.notes: Government subsidizes 50% of premium. Available for food crops and coffee. Penetration still low — only ~3% of Ugandan farmers insured.

programs.name: ACRE Africa Uganda
programs.enrollHow: Bundled with agri-inputs at participating agro-dealers. Ask your seed or fertilizer dealer.
programs.notes: Active in eastern Uganda (maize, common bean). Payout via MTN Mobile Money or Airtel Money.

programs.name: ACRE Africa Rwanda
programs.enrollHow: Available through SACCOs, cooperatives, and agro-dealers. Rwanda Agriculture Board (RAB) partners with ACRE for distribution.
programs.notes: Active in Northern and Eastern Province for maize and common bean. 25% subsidy through RAB. Payout via MTN Mobile Money.

programs.name: Rwanda Cooperative Crop Insurance
programs.enrollHow: Through farming cooperatives (Imirenge cooperatives). Enroll at cooperative office with land title or imidugudu membership.
programs.notes: Government subsidizes 30%. Available through cooperative system — most Rwanda farmers are in cooperatives.

programs.name: Planet Guarantee / AXA CI Agricultural Insurance
programs.provider: Planet Guarantee (AXA partner) + NSIA Côte d'Ivoire
programs.enrollHow: Through Conseil du Café-Cacao for cocoa farmers, or ANADER rural extension services. Ask your cooperative about insurance bundled with inputs.
programs.notes: CIMA regional framework governs agricultural insurance in Côte d'Ivoire. Government subsidizes 30% via Ministère de l'Agriculture.

programs.name: NSIA Cameroun Agricultural Insurance
programs.enrollHow: Apply at NSIA Cameroun offices in Yaoundé, Douala, and regional towns. Also through MINADER agricultural extension offices.
programs.notes: CIMA framework. Bilingual service (French/English). Government subsidizes 25% via MINADER. Covers cocoa, coffee, and food crops.

programs.name: Pula / ACRE Africa Cameroon
programs.enrollHow: Through agro-dealers selling certified seeds. Often bundled — ask when buying Syngenta, Pioneer, or CropLife seeds.
programs.notes: Expanding in northern Cameroon cotton belt and Centre/West cocoa zones.

programs.name: Planet Guarantee / AXA Assurances Sénégal
programs.enrollHow: Through SODAGRI, ANCAR (agri extension), and rural banking institutions. MAER (Ministère de l'Agriculture) subsidizes 40% of premium.
programs.notes: Active in groundnut, millet, and rice belts of Thiès, Diourbel, Kaolack. Payout via Orange Money or Wari.

programs.name: CNAAS Agricultural Insurance
programs.provider: Compagnie Nationale d'Assurance Agricole du Sénégal (CNAAS)
programs.enrollHow: State-owned — apply at CNAAS offices in Dakar, Thiès, Kaolack, Ziguinchor.
programs.notes: State-owned specialized agricultural insurer. Covers all major crops. MAER co-finances premiums.

programs.name: MAMDA Multi-Peril Crop Insurance
programs.enrollHow: Apply at MAMDA branches across Morocco or through Credit Agricole du Maroc. Government (MAPMDREF) subsidizes 80% of premium.
programs.notes: MAMDA is the largest agricultural insurer in Africa — over 700,000 policies. Strongest government support on continent: 80% subsidy. Strategic pillar of Plan Maroc Vert and Generation Green 2020-2030.

programs.name: Assurance Multirisque Climatique (AMC)
programs.enrollHow: Through MAMDA and Crédit Agricole du Maroc branches. Available for cereal farmers.
programs.notes: Very affordable due to 80% subsidy. Index-based — faster payouts than traditional MPCI.

programs.name: CTAMA Crop Insurance
programs.provider: Caisse Tunisienne des Assurances Mutuelles Agricoles (CTAMA)
programs.enrollHow: Apply at CTAMA offices throughout Tunisia. Also accessible through BNA (Banque Nationale Agricole) and BFPME branches.
programs.notes: State-backed mutual insurer. Government subsidizes 65% of premium through Ministry of Agriculture. Long-established program covering olive, cereal, and vegetable sectors.

programs.name: CTAMA Weather Index (Céréales)
programs.enrollHow: Available for wheat and barley farmers through CTAMA and BNA. Specifically designed for smallholder cereal growers.
programs.notes: Index-based product for cereal farmers. Faster payouts. Highly subsidized — farmer pays only 35% of premium.

programs.name: ENSA Angola Agricultural Insurance
programs.provider: ENSA — Empresa Nacional de Seguros e Resseguros de Angola
programs.enrollHow: Apply at ENSA offices in Luanda, Huambo, Huíla, or Malanje. Linked to Instituto de Desenvolvimento Agrário (IDA) credit programs.
programs.notes: Angola's agricultural insurance sector is nascent. Government is actively building the market under the PRODESI diversification program. Premium subsidy of 30% provided through MINAGRIF (Ministério da Agricultura).
